title: The normal distribution
overview: Standardise normal variables to find probabilities, and use the inverse normal to find an unknown value or parameter. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Model a continuous variable with N(μ,σ²).
Standardise and use normal tables/calculator probabilities.
Find unknown values or parameters from probabilities.
Use a continuity-corrected normal approximation to a binomial distribution.

definitions.definition: A symmetric bell-shaped continuous distribution determined by mean μ and variance σ².
Converting X to Z=(X−μ)/σ with distribution N(0,1).
Shifting a discrete boundary by 0.5 when using a continuous approximation.
A value below which a stated proportion of the distribution lies.
σ²; the standard deviation is σ, not σ².

sections.title: Normal model and sketches
content: Write X~N(μ,σ²). The curve is symmetric about μ and total area is 1. Sketch and shade the required tail or interval before standardising; this catches complement and direction errors.
bullets: A point probability is zero for a continuous variable.

sections.title: Standardising
content: For a boundary x, z=(x−μ)/σ. Use Φ(z)=P(Z≤z), symmetry Φ(−z)=1−Φ(z), and differences for intervals. Show the z-expression even when using a calculator directly.
bullets: Retain full precision in z until the final probability.

sections.title: Inverse normal questions
content: Translate the stated area into a standard-normal quantile z, then solve x=μ+zσ. If μ or σ is unknown, each probability gives an equation. Use the sign of z based on whether the boundary lies below or above μ.
bullets: A small lower-tail probability has negative z.

sections.title: Normal approximation to binomial
content: For X~B(n,p), use Y~N(np,npq) when np>5 and nq>5, and apply continuity correction: X≤r becomes Y<r+0.5; X≥r becomes Y>r−0.5.

examTips: Sketch and shade before using normal functions.
Show the continuity-corrected boundary explicitly for approximation questions.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Dividing by variance instead of standard deviation.
Forgetting continuity correction for a discrete-to-continuous approximation.
Using the wrong tail after inverse normal.

quickRecall.question: What is the second parameter in N(μ,σ²)?
Which z corresponds to a boundary below μ?
